claim: In Gravesend, before a blind reviewer, objects standing on counters and an altar's dressing decided what a room was read as: the bare saloon counter read as 'a sauna, a forge or a crypt', the dressed one as a bar; altar dressing was decisive for church against crypt. Printed matter barely registered (most of it was out of frame). The reviewer called one to three props a room 'a small kit': too few, not enough.
evidence: Blind reviewer on Gravesend's town goods, 2026-11-18 (projects/blood-city/experiments/town-goods/README.md and critic.md)
use: Give goods fixtures to stand on (back bar, racks, counters) and dress them first.

checked.how: Read projects/blood-city/experiments/town-goods/README.md: bare saloon counter 'could be a sauna, a forge or a crypt'; 'Props on counters and tables: decisive'; 'Altar dressing: decisive for church versus crypt'; printed matter 'barely' (and mostly out of frame). 'It is a small kit ... Interiors get 1 to 3 props each' (:108, critic.md:49) is the reviewer's complaint, not a finding that one to three is enough: misread, removed.
